chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Ziyad ibn Suqah, from Al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:

I said: What do you say regarding intentional and mistaken acts in killing and wounds? He said: “Mistake is not like intentionality. In intentionality there is killing, and in wounds there is retaliation; but in mistaken killing and wounds there are blood-monies.”

He said, then he said: “O Hakam, when the mistake is from the killer or the one who wounds, and he is a Bedouin, then the blood-money for what the Bedouin has committed by mistake is upon his paternal kin from among the Bedouins.”
He said: “And if the killer or the one who wounds is a townsman, then the blood-money for what he has committed by mistake is upon his paternal kin from among the townspeople.”

key_terms.الدِّيَاتُ: blood-monies or financial compensation due for wrongful harm
key_terms.الْخَطَإِ: mistaken or accidental action lacking deliberate intent
key_terms.الْعَمْدِ: intentional action done deliberately in causing harm
key_terms.الْقِصَاصُ: legal retaliation in kind for intentional injury
key_terms.بَدَوِيًّا: a Bedouin, meaning one belonging to the desert-dwelling community
key_terms.قَرَوِيًّا: a townsman or villager belonging to a settled community

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between intentional and accidental killing and injury in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith distinguishes intentional homicide and injury from accidental cases in legal consequence. Intentional acts entail killing or qisas, while accidental killing and injury entail diyah. It also specifies that liability for accidental harm is borne by the offender’s kin group according to his communal affiliation, whether Bedouin or townsman.
